title: Pages as an async stream
description:
An API returns results a page at a time. Write `public static class Pager` with:

```csharp
public static async IAsyncEnumerable<T> All<T>(Func<int, Task<IReadOnlyList<T>>> fetchPage)
```

It calls `fetchPage(1)`, `fetchPage(2)`, ... and yields every item of each page in order, stopping after the first **empty** page. It must not fetch a page before the items of the previous one have been consumed (so a consumer that stops early stops the fetching too).
hints: An `async` method returning `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` can both `await` and `yield return`. Loop over page numbers, await each page, and `yield break` on an empty one.
Because `yield return` pauses the method until the consumer asks for the next item, the next page is only fetched when the consumer gets that far: laziness comes for free.
